program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s binary question collapses the rubric’s distinction between complete and partial. In the edited image, one frog is clearly inside the bowl, while others are on the lid and floor; the traces consistently identify the bowl frog and report high confidence. Thus the observed evidence supports “complete” under the supplied criterion, not the reference “partial.” Do not force the reference label or treat extra frogs as negating the requested change. Investigate whether the criterion’s phrase “inside the toilet” is being interpreted differently from the intended placement (for example, bowl versus another toilet part), and make the node explicitly assess the rubric’s complete/partial/absent/unknown distinctions with evidence tied to the frog’s position relative to the bowl. The repeated identical yes outputs and 0.99 confidence despite aggregate disagreement indicate a criterion/binding or label-mapping ambiguity, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; no such failures are reported. Preserve uncertainty when placement is genuinely unclear rather than inferring absence.
